title: Don't hide popovers that moved document while hiding a popover stack

labels.name: needs tests
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires someone to write tests

body: Following up on https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/13001. Commit message: --- Don't hide popovers that moved document while hiding a popover stack "Hide popover stack until" works out which popovers to hide before firing any events. If a beforetoggle event listener moved a later popover to another document and showed it there, that popover was still hidden when its turn came. No events were fired for this, even though a toggle event was already queued saying it had opened. The hide popover algorithm now takes an expectedDocument, which it passes to its first call to "check popover validity". It then asserts that the element's node document is expectedDocument and uses that in place of the element's node document for the rest of the algorithm. "Hide popover stack until" passes its document, so popovers that have moved to another document are left alone. In addition, the select element's call to the hide popover algorithm now passes all of its arguments, rather than only the select popover. Follow-up to efc54f7. --- - [x] At least two implementers are interested (and none opposed): * Firefox * Chrome - [x] [Tests](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt) are written and can be reviewed and commented upon at: * https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/63660 - [x] [Implementation bugs](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md#handling-pull-requests) are filed: * Chromium: https://issues.chromium.org/issues/570738049 * Gecko: https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2079362 * WebKit: https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=326681 * Deno (only for timers, structured clone, base64 utils, channel messaging, module resolution, web workers, and web storage): … * Node.js (only for timers, structured clone, base64 utils, channel messaging, and module resolution): … - [ ] Corresponding [HTML AAM](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/) & [ARIA in HTML](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/) issues & PRs: - [ ] [MDN issue](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md#handling-pull-requests) is filed: … - [x] The top of this comment includes a [clear commit message](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/COMMITTING.md) to use.
